currentRouteAndProofGap.policyGap: Authoritative sources define common named-window cutoffs only: 60% of the five-hour quota and 70% of the weekly quota, with equality stopping autonomous admission. They specify repair → quiet-tick → event reviews, account-wide used plus reserved/unknown consumption, and no fraction-of-remainder guarantee. They do not authorize separate numerical cutoffs per work class. The source-required gap is to enforce and demonstrate the ordered pause behavior under the existing shared cutoffs. How work-class order is applied when request upper bounds differ remains an implementation detail for the existing Ops policy; do not invent thresholds. Probe fixture values are test inputs only, not policy authority.

authoritativePolicyEvidence.quote: Ops admission policy is authoritative: autonomous semantic work pauses at ≥ 60% of the 5-hour window or ≥ 70% of the weekly window. Without usage data, a fixed daily job cap applies. Pause order: optional repair → quiet-tick reviews → event reviews. Johan's foreground and its mandatory stop judge are never paused by Toy quota thresholds.

quote: Relevant five-hour window **≥60% used**, or weekly window **≥70% used** | Pause **all autonomous semantic work**: repair/replay/judging, quiet-tick reviews, then event reviews/Continuation; persist deferred work. Equality stops admission. Either window can veto independently.

Approaching a ceiling / outstanding reservations threaten it | Stop optional repair first, then quiet-tick reviews, then event reviews; re-evaluate account-wide usage and reserved/unknown consumption before the next send
Fresh windows below both ceilings | Admit bounded autonomous work within measured headroom, fixed-count/continuation ceilings and one global send lane; foreground always has priority
Missing/stale/unavailable required window | Apply conservative durable **per-day fixed job count**, never estimate a guaranteed percentage reserve; repair/replay remain paused

authoritativePolicyEvidence.quote: - **AT-ops-50 [R0]** Given approaching quota limits, When outstanding reservations and shared-client use reduce headroom, Then optional repair pauses first, quiet-tick reviews next and event reviews/Continuation last, with durable reason/wake state and no shrinking percentage-of-remainder reserve claim.

quote: Ops' named-window thresholds (≥60% five-hour or ≥70% weekly) and conservative cap without reliable data remain protected admission rules. An admission hold checkpoints with a wake.

Foreground and deterministic deadlines precede stop review, normal three-minute review, useful continuation and background repair. Repair starts immediately but yields/checkpoints when foreground needs the model or resources.
Fresh five-hour and weekly windows are recognized by duration, and either equality breach vetoes autonomous work independently of the other window.
Reserve must use one database transaction to bind call key, root budget, run/generation, account, route, policy, named windows/reset, expected cost and work class
and persist either the reservation or denial/wake.
const retryAt = [shortThreat ? short.resetAt : undefined, longThreat ? long.resetAt : undefined].filter(value => value !== undefined).sort().at(-1) ?? null;

minimumWrittenInterfaceAndFiles.interface: The existing per-request reserve/claim owner enforces shared 60%/70% windows but does not own the ordering of known pending work. A future ordered-admission interface must enforce repair/replay -> quiet-tick -> event/Continuation pause order through canonical pending work and retain persisted reasons/wakes without inventing per-class numerical cutoffs. No such interface or fixture is implemented by this plan.
minimumWrittenInterfaceAndFiles.allowedNumericalRule: For measured windows, autonomous admission is denied when (fiveHourUsedPercent + accountWideUnreflectedFiveHourUpperPercent + requestExpectedFiveHourUpperPercent) >= 60, OR (weeklyUsedPercent + accountWideUnreflectedWeeklyUpperPercent + requestExpectedWeeklyUpperPercent) >= 70. The thresholds are fixed absolute provider-window percentages. Without a usable measured window, the existing fixed eight-job UTC-day cap applies; no percentage-of-remainder guarantee is allowed. There are no source-authorized class-specific numeric cutoffs.
minimumWrittenInterfaceAndFiles.unresolvedDesignDetail: The binding sources give no separate numerical cutoff for repair, quiet-tick, event, or Continuation. They require the pause order, but do not specify how the current per-request admission interface should order a set of pending requests whose expected upper bounds differ. Resolve this within the existing Ops policy/owner using the common 60/70 arithmetic; if that interface cannot express the required ordering, identify that exact gap before proposing any extra interface. Test vector percentages must be labeled fixture inputs, not policy constants.

requiredCases.assert: Under the source-defined 60/70 cutoff, use fixture-only shared-usage/reservation/request-cost inputs where repair reaches equality while the later classes remain below it; verify the denial reason and reset wake. The fixture values do not define policy thresholds.

At a later fixture-only shared-usage/reservation state under the same 60/70 cutoff, quiet-tick reaches equality while event/Continuation remain below it; verify the source-required order and persisted reason/reset wake.

When account-wide used plus reserved/unknown plus event/Continuation expected upper bound reaches the common equality ceiling, defer these last and preserve foreground exemption. No separate event-tier cutoff is added.

Vary authorized shared-client usedPercent and durable account-wide outstanding/unknown upper reservations independently; show both reduce headroom against the same 60/70 ceilings, with no reserve recomputed as a fraction of the remainder.
After the existing PostgreSQL restart boundary, ModelAdmission.inspect for each fixture account returns the expected work class, denial reason and exact quota-reset retryAt from the stored record.
